summary: Build continuity plans, test recovery scenarios, and strengthen cyber resilience with practical ISO 22301-aligned training.
lede: Cyber resilience planning helps continuity, security and operations professionals prepare critical services for cyber and technology disruptions. Participants conduct business impact analysis, map dependencies, set recovery priorities, draft incident runbooks and test recovery scenarios. They also develop continuity plans and communicate test findings through resilience reports, dashboards and continuity roadmaps.
audienceIntro: This course is for professionals who must keep critical services running when cyber incidents, technology failures, supplier disruptions, or operational shocks threaten continuity. It is designed for people who own recovery coordination, service restoration, continuity governance, and resilience reporting.
prerequisites: Prerequisites required: working knowledge of IT operations, cybersecurity, service continuity, or risk management; familiarity with incident response processes is helpful. No coding is required. Participants should bring a laptop for workshop templates and scenario exercises, and they should be prepared to work with sample business impact analysis data, recovery priority lists, and continuity plan formats. The course is taught at an intermediate level, with advanced topics such as cyber recovery orchestration covered at a practical awareness level rather than implementation engineering depth.
